Loss of suppression specifically with the dominant-negative construct would support a native CLIC1 requirement; suppression despite the mutant would refute it.

candidate_datasets.name: Long-range Vmem control of tumorigenesis
candidate_datasets.role: published wild-type versus CLIC1C24S contrast, including N=336 for the mutant block

obstacles: Dominant-negative overexpression can disrupt more than CLIC1 conductance.
Expression level and remote voltage for each embryo are not in a public table.
rationale: The wild-type versus point-mutant contrast is a published measurement bearing on whether chloride-driven suppression uses CLIC1. The sample size for the blocking construct is stated. Off-target effects of the dominant-negative protein, and missing per-embryo expression and voltage, leave the requirement claim only partly checked.

operationalization: Under hyperpolarizing high-chloride conditions, express dominant-negative HDAC1 remote from KRASG12D and compare tumor-like-structure incidence with a control construct. An increase near the reported 36% would support an HDAC1 step; no increase, or an increase with HDAC1 activity intact, would refute HDAC1 as the necessary transducer.

candidate_datasets.name: Long-range Vmem control of tumorigenesis
candidate_datasets.role: published 35.6% incidence increase and chi-square result for remote dominant-negative HDAC1

obstacles: A single dominant-negative construct does not show that HDAC1 is the main transducer rather than one contributing factor.
Acetylation and remote voltage were not deposited animal by animal.
rationale: The remote dominant-negative HDAC1 contrast is numerically published and can be checked for direction and reported significance. Calling HDAC1 the main transduction step goes beyond that one intervention. Acetylation readouts that would tie the incidence change to HDAC1 activity are not in a public dataset.

operationalization: Compare oncogene-induced tumor incidence after novobiocin and after the stated gram-positive-targeting cocktail versus vehicle, and pair the incidence change with measured loss of butyrate-producing bacteria. An incidence increase only when those bacteria decline would support the implication; an increase without a microbiome change would leave the bacterial reading unsupported.

candidate_datasets.name: Long-range Vmem control of tumorigenesis
candidate_datasets.role: published 26.2% incidence increase and chi-square result for the antibiotic cocktail

obstacles: Antibiotics change more than gram-positive, butyrate-producing taxa.
Bacterial composition and butyrate were not deposited for these embryo cohorts.
rationale: The incidence increase after the named cocktail is a published contrast with a sample statistic. The inference that native butyrate-producing bacteria normally restrain the tumors is not carried by that contrast alone, because the paper does not include a public microbiome or butyrate measurement for the same animals. Only the incidence half can be inspected now.

operationalization: In the same Xenopus oncogene model, jointly measure remote voltage, butyrate at the prospective tumor site, HDAC1 activity, and tumor incidence under hyperpolarization, antibiotics, and dominant-negative HDAC1. The chain is supported only if incidence tracks butyrate-dependent HDAC1 inhibition downstream of voltage.

candidate_datasets.name: Long-range Vmem control of tumorigenesis
candidate_datasets.role: separate published contrasts for voltage, antibiotics, and dominant-negative HDAC1; the joint butyrate measurement is not included

obstacles: Butyrate concentration in the tadpoles is not a public variable.
The three interventions were not deposited as a single paired dataset that could identify the mediator.
rationale: The mediator claim requires voltage, bacterial butyrate, HDAC1 activity, and tumor incidence in one design. The paper reports related incidence contrasts separately and does not deposit butyrate or acetylation measurements. Biochemical literature on butyrate and HDAC in other systems does not supply this Xenopus chain.

operationalization: Record bioelectric signals at a distance from induced tumors, with connectivity intact and interrupted, and test whether a remote signature predicts tumor state and disappears when the path is cut. A connectivity-dependent remote signature would support outward emission; no remote signal above controls would refute it.
obstacles: The emitted signal and the distance at which it should be detectable are unspecified.
No public dataset pairs remote non-neural voltage with these induced structures.
rationale: Outward bioelectric emission is testable once a remote signal and a disconnection control are defined, which the speculation leaves open. No deposited recording set contains that pair for the Xenopus structures or a mammalian counterpart. The detection claim therefore waits on new measurements.

operationalization: Match the degree of hyperpolarization achieved by a potassium channel and by chloride loading, and test whether tumor suppression follows voltage rather than channel identity. Equal suppression at equal voltage, and loss of suppression when voltage is clamped back, would support the systems-level claim.

candidate_datasets.name: Long-range Vmem control of tumorigenesis
candidate_datasets.role: published suppression by both Kv1.5 and high-chloride hyperpolarization in the same Xenopus assay

obstacles: The two treatments were not published as voltage-matched dose responses.
Chloride loading and potassium-channel expression can share non-voltage effects.
rationale: Suppression by two different ionic routes is published and is the right kind of evidence for a voltage-level rather than a channel-identity cause. The summaries are not a voltage-matched series, and raw voltages are not public. The Xenopus contrasts therefore speak to part of the general causal claim and leave the matched test incomplete.

operationalization: Map butyrate-producing bacteria, surface charge or membrane voltage, local butyrate, histone acetylation, and cell-cycle state across hyperpolarized host tissue and depolarized oncogene cells. Skew of viable bacteria and butyrate toward the depolarized cells, with HDAC inhibition there, would support the spatial model.
obstacles: No public spatial microbiome or butyrate map exists for these tadpoles.
Bacterial attachment and bacterial viability can respond differently to surface charge, so both need to be measured.
rationale: The proposed skew of butyrate-producing bacteria toward depolarized oncogene cells is a spatial prediction with chemical and histological readouts. Those maps were not deposited with the incidence results, and general butyrate–HDAC datasets from other species lack the embryo geometry. The distribution model needs new or newly released measurements.

operationalization: In mammalian tumor models, change resting potential of host tissue remote from the tumor, preferably with clinically used channel drugs, and test detection and tumor-growth endpoints against voltage-clamped controls. Conservation would appear as a remote-voltage effect on detection or growth; its absence in adequately powered models would refute conservation.

candidate_datasets.name: IUPHAR/BPS Guide to Pharmacology
candidate_datasets.role: catalog of ion-channel drugs, including agents already used in humans, without remote-voltage cancer outcomes

obstacles: Mammalian studies do not publicly pair remote host Vmem with tumor incidence under these interventions.
Approved channel drugs have extensive non-voltage pharmacology, so a clinical association would not identify the Xenopus mechanism.
rationale: The prediction is conditional on conservation in mammalian models and on a therapeutic effect of voltage modulation. Channel-drug catalogs list candidate reagents and do not contain the remote-voltage experiments. Cancer genomics portals likewise lack this physiological exposure, so the conservation claim still requires new mammalian data.

operationalization: Score stage-45 tadpoles for absent nostrils, forebrain, or midbrain and for misformed hindbrain after 0.1 mg/mL nicotine from stages 10 to 35, against untreated siblings. A major-defect rate near 55% versus near 6% in controls would support the result; overlapping rates would refute it.

candidate_datasets.name: HCN2 voltage pre-patterns
candidate_datasets.role: published approximate incidence contrast and scoring criteria; individual embryo scores are available from the authors on request rather than as an open file

obstacles: The data-availability statement leaves raw scores with the corresponding author.
The published rates are approximate, and nicotine has several targets besides the brain-voltage pattern.
rationale: The defect classes, dose, stages, and approximate rates are explicit published measurements. They can be checked for a large treated-versus-control gap. Because the embryo-level scores and images are not openly deposited, the percentages cannot be recomputed or audited for scoring bias, which leaves the result partly resolvable.

operationalization: Rebuild the stage-15 anterior neurula in BETSE with the published ion concentrations, regional potassium and chloride leak, and Kir conductance, and test whether neural-tube Vmem is near −50 mV while folds and ectoderm stay near −5 mV. Closing Kir, or equalizing the leaks, should remove that contrast if the stated mechanism is required.
